# END_TO_END_WORKFLOW_MAP

**Repository:** github.com/shmuelbiller1/ledgerflow · **Pinned revision:** `9aed5466c469` (`9aed5466c4691c5c55c6d4dbec0565d88dbc8462`)
**Generated by:** `work/genworkflows.mjs` (audit-only, not part of the application).

## How this map was built and how far it is verified

- The 18 base workflows are the project's own Code Intelligence Atlas entries (`docs/CODE_ATLAS.jsonl`, built at `74b8318b…`). They were **re-verified against the pinned revision** by `work/reverify_workflows.mjs`: every one of the **215 file/symbol references was re-resolved on disk** — 0 missing files, 0 missing symbols, 2 line-number drifts (`recategorize` moved from line 49 to 32; `exportWorkspaceBackup` from 173 to 186).
- Two workflows (**WF-19** daily automation, **WF-20** document delivery) were added because the Atlas has no entry for them. They are existing paths, but this audit records open reliability/scope gaps; they are not certified end to end.
- **Status vocabulary** used below: `SOURCE-TRACED (no confirmed defect in inspected slice)` means the listed path was traced in current source; it is not a full browser/DB end-to-end pass. `SOURCE-TRACED WITH FINDING(S)` means a defect/risk was confirmed on an inspected boundary. `PARTIAL` means a path is incomplete or has an unverified operational boundary. `BROKEN` means a demonstrated defect produces a wrong result. These labels do not imply all branches, providers or deployment databases were exercised.
- Independent execution evidence for this map: the configured unit-test command (2,799 tests passed, 0 failed) plus the audit probes listed in `VERIFIED_BUG_REPORT.md`. The unit run emitted 125 `LF_TEST_DATABASE_URL not set` notices; no real-PostgreSQL/RLS run was performed. TAP reported zero leaf skips, which is not database coverage.

## WF-19 — Daily automation: recurring documents, reminders, statements, scheduled reports, watches, alerts, retention

- **Id:** `WF-19` (added by this audit; no Atlas entry exists)
- **Status:** PARTIAL
- **What this audit independently checked:** `cronRouter` (src/server/routes/cronRoutes.ts) mounts 14 daily jobs behind a timing-safe `CRON_SECRET` compare; `vercel.json` schedules `/api/cron/daily` at 06:10; each job is run in sequence, a failure is caught per job, recorded in `jobRuns` and reported as HTTP 500. The Settings → Schedule screen reads that record and is deliberately read-only.
- **Findings on this path:** AUD-04 (source-confirmed): `src/server/services/scheduledReportService.ts:92` writes the `scheduledReportsSent.<id>` marker BEFORE the send. A send that then fails is not retried on that period; no concurrent-claim/real-mail run was made. AUD-05: standalone `serveApp.ts` periodic work does not include the full `cronRoutes.ts` registry used by Vercel.

**Stage trace:**

- **entry**
  - Vercel Cron → `GET /api/cron/daily` (vercel.json `crons[0]`, 10 6 * * *)
- **inputs**
  - `CRON_SECRET` bearer token; workspace records selected inside each job
- **calculation**
  - `recurringService.processAllRecurring`, `reminderService.runDailyReminders` / `runDailyStatements`, `scheduledReportService.runDailyScheduledReports`, `watchService.runDailyWatches`, `retentionService.runDailyRetention`, `notificationService.runNotificationJobs`
- **action**
  - Each job writes its own documents / sends its own mail
- **persistence**
  - `jobRuns.daily_latest` via `recordDailyJobRun`; per-workspace sent markers
- **verification**
  - src/tests/recurring-job.test.ts, reminders-job.test.ts, scheduled-reports.test.ts (DB suites — skipped here without Postgres)
